name: Eric M Demarco
current_role: President, CEO and Director, Kratos Defense & Security Solutions (NASDAQ: KTOS)
profile: Eric DeMarco joined Wireless Facilities Inc. in 2003 as President/COO and became CEO in April 2004, transforming it into Kratos, a national-security technology firm in drones, hypersonics, space, propulsion and microwave electronics. Previously President/COO of Titan Corporation. His wealth comes from Kratos equity.
interesting_fact: He led Kratos' pivot from a commercial wireless-infrastructure services company to a defense-tech maker of jet-powered unmanned aircraft (e.g. the XQ-58 Valkyrie), hypersonic systems and satellite ground systems.
deep_cut_fact: Before defense, he started in public accounting; at Titan Corporation he helped grow annualized revenue from about $150M to $1.5B. He graduated summa cum laude from the University of New Hampshire (B.S. business administration & finance) and sits on the Aerospace Industries Association's Board of Governors.
notes: Press contact Claire Cantrell is listed on Kratos releases; IR phone 877-934-4687. Frequent CEO interviewee (TWST, earnings calls) on defense/drones.

name: Ryan Pardo
current_role: Chief Legal Officer and Corporate Secretary, LifeStance Health Group (NASDAQ: LFST)
profile: Ryan Pardo has been Chief Legal Officer of LifeStance Health, one of the largest US outpatient mental-health providers, since 2017, and was part of the team through its 2021 IPO. Earlier he was General Counsel of Liberty Dialysis until its 2012 sale to Fresenius, and co-founded Liberty Health Partners (merged into Signify Health). Wealth stems from LifeStance equity.
interesting_fact: A healthcare-services dealmaker: he was GC at Liberty Dialysis through its acquisition by Fresenius Medical Care, then worked in M&A/business development for Fresenius before joining LifeStance.
deep_cut_fact: Before healthcare he was Corporate Counsel at outdoor retailer Eddie Bauer, leading its securities reporting before the going-private deal, and earlier practiced corporate finance law at Dorsey & Whitney. He studied economics at Stanford and earned his J.D. at Harvard Law School.
notes: Legal executive, low public profile; 'See Remarks' insider title = CLO. Little relevance to energy/data centers. IR contact Monica Prokocki (VP Finance & IR); media contact Brooke Matthews (Sr. Director Communications) per releases.

name: Julian Forrest Barnwell Jr.
current_role: President & CEO, Design and Production Inc. (Lorton, VA); Director, Burke & Herbert Financial Services Corp. (NASDAQ: BHRB) since 2001
profile: J. Forrest Barnwell Jr. has led Design and Production Inc. (D&P), one of the largest US museum-exhibit fabricators, since 1991, and has been a director of Northern Virginia lender Burke & Herbert since 2001. His insider holdings are in Burke & Herbert stock (several hundred thousand shares, partly held in family trusts).
interesting_fact: His firm D&P, founded in 1949 and celebrating 75 years in 2024, builds exhibits for presidential, military, natural-history and state museums; in 2018 alone it opened the Bell Museum, Tennessee State Museum and National Law Enforcement Museum.
deep_cut_fact: D&P, the company he runs, helped create the 1970s 'Treasures of Tutankhamen' (King Tut) blockbuster exhibition, and in the 1960s invented the 'Sho Coach', a customizable tractor-trailer traveling museum that toured the country.
notes: Bank director role is via Form 4/proxy (Burke & Herbert 10-K 2023: director since 2001, age 68 then). Contact email is D&P's general marketing inbox, not personal. Private, low public profile; relevance to podcast is as a family-business/manufacturing owner.

name: Vinay S. Kumar
current_role: Chief Product & Technology Officer, DigitalOcean (NYSE: DOCN), since January 2026
profile: Vinay Kumar joined DigitalOcean as CPTO in January 2026 to lead product, engineering, cloud infrastructure and security as the company pushes into AI inference cloud. He spent a decade-plus at Oracle (from 2015), helping build Oracle Cloud Infrastructure from its earliest days into a hyperscale platform, after earlier roles at AWS, Akamai and Dell/EMC.
interesting_fact: He was an early/founding leader of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, helping grow it from inception into a global hyperscale cloud before moving to DigitalOcean to build its AI inference platform.
deep_cut_fact: Before Oracle he led product management for AWS core storage services, including Elastic Block Store (EBS) and S3. He trained as an electronics & communication engineer at Bangalore University and later earned an MBA at Babson College.
notes: Highly relevant to data-center/AI-cloud theme (OCI hyperscale buildout, DigitalOcean AI inference cloud). Oracle exec page may be stale/removed after his departure; deep-cut details are from it (fetched via search summary, page 403s to curl).

name: John W Lindsay
current_role: Senior Advisor (through Dec 2026), Helmerich & Payne (H&P); retired as CEO/director March 4, 2026; director of Arcosa, Inc. (status post-CRH deal unverified)
profile: John Lindsay spent his whole career at Tulsa-based land driller Helmerich & Payne, joining in 1987 as a drilling engineer and serving as CEO from 2014 to March 2026. He led H&P through shale-era cycles and the pandemic, scaled the FlexRig fleet and bought five technology companies. Now a senior advisor to successor Trey Adams through 2026.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership H&P became the world's leading land driller; he championed the FlexRig, the rig design that helped reshape US shale drilling, and pushed H&P into automation and directional-drilling software via five tech acquisitions.
deep_cut_fact: He started at H&P in 1987 as a drilling engineer and spent nearly 40 years at the one company, rising through VP U.S. Land Operations (1997-2006) and EVP U.S. & International Operations before becoming CEO in 2014.
notes: Recently retired CEO, may be more available for podcasts in 2027. Very relevant to energy theme. Arcosa IR pages now redirect to CRH, suggesting Arcosa was acquired; his Arcosa board seat may have ended (unverified).
